question: What is the main goal of a hospital Quality Assurance Committee?

options.A: Monitoring and improving clinical care quality
options.B: Managing hospital finances and staff salaries
options.C: Procuring medical drugs and heavy equipment
options.D: Recruiting new doctors and nursing officers

explanation: The committee specifically targets clinical excellence and patient safety rather than general administrative finances or human resource recruitment. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h1)

question: How do hospital QA committees function within the broader health system?

options.A: They manage external relations with health insurance companies
options.B: They act as a legal court for punishing erring staff
options.C: They replace the nursing and medical directors entirely
options.D: They translate national health policies into daily ward practices

explanation: QA committees serve as the operational link between high-level health guidelines and actual bedside clinical execution. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h1)

question: Who typically represents bedside nursing care on the hospital QA committee?
explanation: The nursing leadership represents ward-level care, nursing standards, and patient safety protocols on the committee. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why must a Quality Assurance Committee include members from multiple departments?

options.A: It prevents any single department from having executive power
options.B: Government labor laws mandate equal representation for all health unions
options.C: Doctors alone refuse to take responsibility for hospital errors
options.D: Patient care involves multiple departments whose coordination affects safety

explanation: Healthcare delivery is team-based, requiring input from nursing, pharmacy, laboratory, and medicine to catch system gaps. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is a primary duty of the Quality Assurance Committee?

options.B: Building new wards and hospital wings
options.C: Disbursing monthly salaries to hospital staff
options.D: Conducting regular clinical audits and reviews

explanation: Clinical audits and mortality reviews form the core evaluative responsibilities of a QA committee. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h3)

question: How should a QA committee handle a serious clinical error in the hospital?

options.A: Report the case directly to the national police force
options.B: Investigate systemic root causes rather than blaming individuals
options.C: Immediately terminate the employment of the attending nurse
options.D: Hide the incident from the public to protect the hospital name

explanation: Effective quality improvement looks at systemic flaws that allowed the error to happen, fostering a safe reporting culture. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which indicator is a nurse member most likely to track for clinical quality?

options.A: Frequency of board of directors meetings
options.B: Total annual revenue generated by the pharmacy
options.C: Cost of maintaining hospital transport vehicles
options.D: Pressure ulcer and patient fall rates

explanation: Pressure ulcers and falls are direct markers of nursing care quality and ward safety compliance. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: A sudden increase in surgical site infections in a theatre prompts the committee to do what?

options.A: Blame the surgical patients for poor personal hygiene
options.B: Initiate a focused investigation into sterilization and aseptic protocols
options.C: Ignore the data as a normal statistical fluctuation
options.D: Immediately shut down the entire hospital for fumigation

explanation: Unusual spikes in adverse outcomes demand systematic reviews of equipment, environment, and procedural compliance. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of incident reporting within a healthcare facility?

options.B: Finding guilty staff members to administer punishment
options.C: Creating legal documents for court litigation cases
options.D: Identifying system vulnerabilities to prevent future harm

explanation: Incident reporting exists to uncover hidden system flaws and prevent the same mistake from recurring. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why do healthcare workers often fail to report near-misses in clinical settings?

options.A: Fear of disciplinary action or punitive measures
options.B: Absence of sick leave for clinical personnel
options.C: Strict orders from the national nursing council
options.D: Lack of interest in patient safety improvement

explanation: A punitive work culture drives errors underground; staff will not report mistakes if they fear losing their jobs. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: What does KPI stand for in healthcare quality assurance?
explanation: KPI stands for Key Performance Indicator, used to measure institutional success against established standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is accurate daily nursing documentation vital for the QA committee?

options.A: It protects the hospital from paying annual taxes
options.B: It replaces the need for formal staff performance appraisals
options.C: It provides reliable data for analyzing hospital performance trends
options.D: It is only required for billing patients at discharge

explanation: Accurate ward records are the raw data source the committee uses to evaluate patient outcomes and safety. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary difference between corrective and preventive actions?

options.A: Corrective requires government approval while preventive does not
options.B: Corrective is for doctors while preventive is for nurses
options.C: Corrective fixes existing errors while preventive stops future ones
options.D: Corrective costs money while preventive is completely free

explanation: Corrective actions address past failures, whereas preventive actions stop potential future failures from occurring. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the final crucial step after implementing a quality action plan in a hospital?

options.A: Publishing the failure on national television news
options.B: Evaluating whether the intervention successfully solved the problem
options.C: Filing the incident report away in a locked cabinet
options.D: Suspending all clinical staff involved in the original error

explanation: Follow-up evaluation ensures that the changes made actually improved patient safety and closed the quality loop. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge for QA committees in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Erratic power supply affecting clinical records
options.C: Excessive financial surplus and surplus equipment

explanation: Nigerian hospitals typically face severe resource shortages and funding gaps, not financial surpluses. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)

question: How can hospital management best overcome staff resistance to new quality protocols?

options.A: By keeping all new quality guidelines a secret from ward staff
options.B: By threatening immediate dismissal for non-compliance
options.C: By outsourcing all nursing duties to foreign agencies
options.D: By involving staff in planning and providing adequate training

explanation: Engagement and education reduce resistance, helping staff take ownership of the new safety standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h8)
